source.title: The Hidden Width of Deep ResNets: Tight Error Bounds and Phase Diagrams

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices and version notes. No truncation or garbling prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own gradient-training experiments on toy residual networks and analyzes their training dynamics against a Neural Mean ODE. It tests aspects of training behavior and width/depth scaling, but not benchmark classification error as stated in the versions.
record.gate_note: Reported toy experiments measure mean-square loss and approximation error to a limit model. These bear on whether training progresses in the tested setting, but do not test CIFAR classification error, random-label fitting, depth-related training error degradation, shortcuts versus plain networks, initialization comparisons, learning-rate stability thresholds, or batch normalization. Cited findings from other papers are not rows. Loss curves and rate comparisons shown only in figures are not extracted as numeric rows.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes residual-network dynamics and approximation to infinite-depth limits. Its toy regression loss, output-approximation errors and feature-update scalings do not test any stated version. Initialization-dependent feature updates are distinct from V4's training-speed and trainable-depth claims for plain networks; its stable learning-rate scalings do not test V5's curvature thresholds or recovery.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate but needs qualifications: at fixed embedding dimension and fixed gradient-step horizon, appropriately scaled randomly initialized ResNets approach a Neural Mean ODE regardless of hidden-width scaling. A separate lazy-ODE scaling approaches a tangent Mean ODE. Explicit dimension-dependent bounds for two-layer perceptron blocks require clipping and shape assumptions. Toy experiments support the predicted approximation rates; these are not guarantees of convergence to a training optimum.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes and experimentally validates toy ResNet training dynamics using mean-square loss and output approximation to a Neural Mean ODE, rather than benchmark classification error or the interventions named in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The approximation bound depends on depth L, hidden width M, embedding dimension D, residual scale, and—in the 2LP theorem—clipping assumptions and shape conditions. The paper distinguishes maximal-local-update and lazy-ODE regimes by residual scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: The Mean ODE proxy's squared training loss is described as near zero after 100 gradient steps on 10 random input/output pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The studied toy residual model can approximately fit a small random regression dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Output distances to the Mean ODE agree with predicted depth, width and embedding-dimension approximation rates in the tested regimes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite ResNet training dynamics approximate their infinite-depth limit at the predicted rates over fixed training horizons.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4.2 derives initialization and learning-rate scalings separating maximal local feature updates from vanishing local updates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual scaling controls local feature learning in the studied ResNet asymptotic regimes.

record.problems: The empirical validation is in basic toy settings using only 10 random input/output pairs and mean-square loss; it does not evaluate benchmark classification or the claim versions' settings. Key experimental values are figures rather than explicitly stated numbers. Theoretical convergence claims are for a fixed number of gradient steps and do not establish zero classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No cited prior-work results were extracted. Figure-only approximation-rate experiments were retained as rows, but numeric values could not be recovered from the text. No classification-error result is reported.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and size or recipe dependencies.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and their reduction through extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation, plain versus residual comparisons, and the special-initialization and Fixup results.
Activation-matched initialization effects on plain-network training speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Loss recovery, curvature adaptation, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and equivalent training with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The text contains no separate conclusion section. The abstract, contribution summary, experimental sections and theorem qualifications establish the scope. Background citations to original sources do not constitute tests.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 classification error; corrupted or random labels; comparisons by model size, early stopping, or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks' training error by depth on ImageNet or CIFAR-10; plain tanh training by special initialization; Fixup training without normalization.
Comparisons among initialization schemes for signal or gradient propagation, trainability, speed, or 10,000-layer networks.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, loss rises and recovery, sharpness, or divergence.
Batch normalization versus no normalization for training speed, accuracy, or learning-rate tolerance; Fixup comparisons.

conditions.value: 10 input/output pairs with N(0, 1) iid entries

rows.note: The text says the Mean ODE loss is close to 0 at k = 100, indicating approximate convergence. The value is shown only in a figure.
rows.check: Near-zero regression loss cannot establish any version's effect, so partial is inappropriate. Figure 3a represents the Mean ODE using a finite ResNet proxy with M = L = 1000; record that implementation and the text's stated near-zero loss at step 100, although an exact value is unavailable.
